transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-12-09 14:30 PST | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Aisha, Marcus, Priya, Tom (Redwood) — Laura, Ben, Sophie, Ravi (Pendulum)

Summary: quick intro, scope POC that runs inside Pendulum VPC with either peering or Privatelink. security wants no cross-region egress, limited outbound CIDRs, and collector logs to stay in customer account.

00:00:06 Aisha (AE, Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round table — Laura, Ben, Sophie, Ravi, can you confirm you're the right folks for networking and security?
00:00:14 Laura (CTO, Pendulum): Yep hi this is Laura. Ben is infra, Sophie on security, Ravi does data pipelines. we also pulled in an intern for notes.
00:00:22 Ben (Infra Lead): hi, hi.
00:00:25 Marcus (SE, Redwood): quick agenda — we'll cover connectivity options, residency requirements, how we'll run benches, and success criteria. then assign action items and timelines.
00:00:37 Sophie (Security Architect): just flag up front: SOC2 in progress, we need audit logs, SSO integration, and most importantly no egress outside eu-west-1 for prod data. pilot can be in us-west-2 if necessary but must remain in-region for production.
00:00:55 Priya (Solutions Eng, Redwood): noted. For pilot we'll propose a fenced VPC in eu-west-1 — either peering into Redwood's dedicated endpoint or Privatelink endpoint inside your account. both are workable; tradeoffs to discuss.

00:01:12 Ben: can you run through the peering vs privatelink differences again? costs, routing, management?
00:01:18 Marcus: yeah, short version — VPC peering gives direct network path, simpler routing but you need cross-account route management and potential route table complexity. Privatelink (interface endpoints) gives an ENI inside your subnet, no route table changes, easier security posture, but small per-hour endpoint costs and slightly higher latency in some configs. Also Privatelink only uses AWS backbone to the service and limits exposure of our control plane.
00:01:47 Laura: latency matters — we do 200ms p50 tail-to-tail on our current service and can't add more than ~30ms overhead for inference calls. what's realistic?
00:01:57 Marcus: for typical text-generation workloads over peering we'd expect 8–20ms additional network hop; with privatelink maybe 12–30ms depending on ENI placement and NACLs. but main latencies come from model host time, not the pipe. we'll test with your payloads.
00:02:18 Ravi: payloads vary—some small prompts (avg 80 tokens), some long chain-of-thought debugging logs (avg 2,400 tokens). QPS target for pilot: 15 sustained, burst to 60 for short windows.
00:02:33 Priya: good data. For bench we need representative inputs: small, medium, large. Also measure cold-starts when KV-caches are cold, and warm-path tokens/sec.
00:02:45 Sophie: also, outgoing egress — we cannot allow calls to leave eu-west-1 for the prod dataset. pilot can be eu-west-1 or us-west-2 but we will confirm. If you use a multi-region fallback you'll need explicit approval and audit logs to show where tokens went.
00:03:02 Tom (CSM): we'll include detailed audit logging and a per-request region tag so you can trace. Redwood's control plane metadata can be forwarded to your SIEM via a customer-managed Kinesis/S3 — we'll include that in the runbook.

00:03:22 Laura: curious about data at rest — if we cache embeddings or prefixes, where does that live? in your infra or ours?
00:03:29 Marcus: we have two options: cache in our managed layer (we can enable encryption with customer KMS, but keys live in Redwood unless you do private deployment), or cache inside your VPC with an ENI-backed cache that keeps data fully inside your account. For pilot we'll propose the in-account cache to satisfy compliance.

00:03:50 Ben: ok that pushes me toward Privatelink with an in-VPC cache. but I'm worried about egress flows from model artifact downloads — sometimes the model starts in object storage outside the region for cold-start. can you pin models and artifacts to eu-west-1?
00:04:03 Marcus: yes — for private deployments we can pin model blobs to a provisioning bucket in eu-west-1; for hosted we can pin to region-specific variants. there may be occasional control-plane calls for metrics, but we'll make them optional and document them.

00:04:21 Sophie: we need an allowlist for outbound CIDRs. who owns that?
00:04:25 Aisha: Redwood will provide the minimal set of CIDRs and FQDNs required for the pilot (for health checks, hero endpoints). we'll also provide a privatelink ALB endpoint IP set you can use for NACLs. Marcus will follow up with the exact list.

00:04:40 Marcus: action: we'll supply three things — ephemeral CIDR list for bench, terraform snippet for Privatelink or peering, and a perf harness that can run from your VPC with results to a shared S3.

00:04:52 Ravi: about benchmarks — we want p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and SLO breach rate. also memory/CPU consumption on our side? we need host metrics to understand scaling.
00:05:03 Priya: we'll instrument the bench to push model metrics and give you per-request timing. We'll also provide a dashboard template showing p50/p95, 90th/99th percentiles, token throughput, and cost estimate per 1k tokens.

00:05:19 Laura: success criteria — what should we agree to that says pilot succeeded?
00:05:24 Aisha: good question. proposed success criteria for pilot: 1) in-region data residency (all inference request/response and caches remain in eu-west-1) — pass/fail; 2) latency overhead from network <= 30ms p50 and <= 60ms p95 measured over a 24-hour steady state with 15 qps; 3) model quality parity — no regression on our 10 curated prompts (we'll run the eval set and track MRR/ROUGE as agreed); 4) cost per 1k tokens within a predefined target (Redwood will estimate); 5) operational runbook completed and validated (privatelink + allowlist applied and rollback steps tested).
00:06:05 Sophie: we need a clause for residual exfil attempts — if any downstream call attempts to outside-CIDR, it should be blocked and an alert created. audit trail must show the blocked event.
00:06:17 Tom: Redwood can push logs to your S3 and trigger CloudWatch alarms. we'll include an alerting template.

00:06:27 Ben: pilot sizing — what infra are you going to allocate?
00:06:30 Marcus: for the pilot we'll reserve a 2-GPU pool (A10G equivalent) with burst to 4 GPUs for peak windows. That should cover 15 qps with your medium model (we'll confirm model size), and handle cold starts. If your payloads are heavier (2.4k tokens) we may need quantized variants — Marcus will propose quantization profile and model shard count.
00:06:55 Ravi: is there any chance to test with a smaller model first? we might run with a 7B for bench then evaluate 13B.
00:07:02 Priya: absolutely. We'll run a step-up bench: 7B baseline, then 13B, then customer-picked model. That helps us isolate model-hosting costs and latency delta.

00:07:14 Sophie: timeline? we need this done before Q1 procurement review on 2028-01-20.
00:07:20 Aisha: proposed timeline: onboarding docs and runbook shared by 2027-12-11, customer provides workloads by 2027-12-13, bench run 2027-12-16 to 2027-12-17, review 2027-12-20, outcomes to procurement by 2028-01-10. That fits your procurement date.
00:07:39 Laura: ok sounds reasonable. who signs off for prod residency?
00:07:43 Sophie: security will sign the runbook if audit logs and KMS integration are acceptable. CTO signoff after security.

00:07:50 Ben: about Privatelink costs — you mentioned small per-hour endpoint fees. can you give a rough estimate for pilot?
00:07:56 Marcus: rough calc: interface endpoint per AZ ~ $0.01-$0.02 per hour plus data processing costs, maybe $30–$100 per month for the pilot depending on bandwidth. We'll provide a more accurate estimate once we know throughput.
00:08:12 Ravi: will Redwood push model updates without our approval? we need version pinning in pilot.
00:08:18 Priya: by default we allow pinning — pilot will be pinned to a model version you approve. Redwood Optimize suggestions are advisory and require opt-in.

00:08:28 Laura: ok good. now the bench specifics — I want the harness to run 24-hour steady-state and a soak test with bursts. include cold-start windows and measure p95 during cold starts.
00:08:39 Marcus: yes. bench phases: 1) functional smoke (sanity), 2) steady-state 24h at 15 qps, 3) burst tests (60 qps for 10 min every 4 hours), 4) cold-start ramp (scale from 0 to required) and measure tail latency. We'll capture telemetry and raw traces.

00:09:00 Sophie: for compliance we'll need a runbook entry that explains how to revoke endpoints and rotate keys.
00:09:07 Marcus: included. For Privatelink we have a documented revoke path and a terraform snippet for quick teardown. We'll also show KMS key rotation steps.

00:09:20 Laura: what about model artifact provenance — we need a record of model weights origin and checksum.
00:09:26 Priya: we'll provide checksums and attestations for any model we serve for you. If you run private deployment we can surface the artifact manifest in your bucket.

00:09:36 Ben: firewall rules — we will implement NACLs that block 0.0.0.0/0 outbound except allowed CIDRs. will Redwood require any dynamic IPs?
00:09:43 Aisha: all dynamic ranges will be via service discovery FQDNs and for pilot we can provide static ENI IPs for privatelink. so no dynamic outbound to arbitrary IPs.

00:09:55 Ravi: how will we validate residency? is it line-item evidence?
00:09:59 Tom: Redwood will provide per-request region metadata and S3-stored logs that show source IP/ENI, region tag, and the model shard location. that's the evidence you can attach to an audit.

00:10:13 Sophie: good, need that for SOC2 scope. Also add tests for dropped packets and retransmits in bench to emulate network hiccups.
00:10:22 Marcus: we'll add a chaos step with 2% packet loss window to see impact on latency and retries.

00:10:30 Laura: any blockers from your side?
00:10:33 Aisha: none from Redwood — we just need the sample payloads and CIDR policy. Also need a point of contact for AWS account ops for endpoint creation.
00:10:43 Ben: that's me. I'll work with Marcus on the terraform snippet.

00:10:49 Priya: ok, to recap and close — deliverables: runbook + privatelink vs peering matrix (Aisha by 12/11), sample payload spec (Ben by 12/13), benchmark harness and terraform snippet (Marcus by 12/15), bench window scheduled (12/16-12/17), post-bench review 12/20.
00:11:10 Laura: yep. and final acceptance criteria: in-region residency, latency thresholds, no data leakage, cost within budget, runbook validated.
00:11:22 Aisha: thanks all. we'll follow up in email with calendar invites and attach the runbook draft.
00:11:29 Speaker 1 (intern): thanks everyone, bye.

00:11:35 End of recorded portion. Partial auto-summary and action items appended.

Transcript notes: occasional words mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache -> K-V cash), speaker attribution approximated where more than two speakers spoke over each other. There were short cross-talk segments when bench phases and timelines were discussed.
